coordinates: mm; X right, Y forward, Z up; heading clockwise from +Y (CAD Z rotation = -heading)

profile.section_status: Generic visual T-slot section; actual purchased profile cross-section, alloy, end taps and stiffness need verification.

lidar_mount.rev17b_note: Rev17b: 3D-printed pedestal replaces the 3t sheet bracket (vibration): solid from the base-plate top to the scanner bottom, two 6 mm walls 55 mm up the column faces (3 M5 T-nut bolts each), 3 M5 bolts into the base plate, scanner 2x M3 from below
lidar_mount.rev17_note: Rev17 (vibration): flanges go 55 mm up the column (3 M5 T-nut bolts each, pattern 39 mm vs 16 mm) and the sensor plate gets 15 mm downturned lips on its edges; scanner held by 2x M3x5 into its 2.8 mm bottom threads (SICK, 0.8 N m max; hole spacing assumed until the SICK drawing is checked)
lidar_mount.optical_datum_status: 62.46 above body-bottom reference from SICK drawing; 15.37 connector allowance derived from101.12-85.75. Translating these to this simplified centered envelope is a layout assumption; verify actual optical origin and ROS TF.
lidar_mount.fov_status: 270 degrees aimed outward; blind90 toward chassis. Geometric sampling only, no safety certification or guaranteed detection.
lidar_mount.rev17e_note: Rev17e (user): scanner bottom Z163 -> 129 so the scan plane (Z206.83) equals eco; the printed base (9 mm on the 3t base plate, 12 mm deeper skirt where it overhangs the plate edge) is fixed to the base plate only by 3x M5 from above on its inboard tongue, outside the scanner, nuts under the plate; the column walls and column bolts are gone

camera_mount.wedge_status: Rev17e: printed hanger with a 5 mm back plate; the camera is fixed by 2x M2 through it into the camera rear threads (pitch 80, official 2D V1.2)

hanger.note: Rev17b: one printed hanger per camera replaces the 2020 hanger column, the 3t adapter plate and the loose wedge

electronics.driver_note: driver_x/y/center_z are the Rev05-Rev16 twin-driver dummies (baseline only). Rev17 uses motor_driver

motor_driver.mount: Rev17: wide side down directly on the 3t steel base plate (heat spreader, thermal pad), 4x M3x10 through the corner ears + nylock under the plate (manual 2.4: wide-side mounting uses M3 through the four corner holes; narrow side is recommended for heat - check the temperature on the prototype)
motor_driver.electrical: Input 20-48 VDC (typ. 36), output current 15 A typical / 30 A peak per channel, over-voltage 60 V, under-voltage 16 V; hall U/V/W + incremental encoder A/B inputs, 5 V supply to encoder and hall; CANopen (CiA301/402, 25-1000 kbps) and RS485 Modbus-RTU; 2 programmable opto inputs; 0-50 C
motor_driver.source: ZLAC8015D Servo Driver Manual (Special for Hub Servo Motor) V1.0, ZLTECH (www.zlingkj.com): 2.1 electrical index, 2.2 environment, Fig.1 installation dimension 168 x 89 x 29.7 (body 158, side hole pitch 42). Corner-hole pitch not dimensioned in the figure (envelope only)
motor_driver.fit_to_motor: ZLLG65ASM250-N V2: 24 V, 10 A rated / 30 A stall, 1024-line magnetic A/B encoder + hall. ZLTECH lists ZLAC8015/ZLAC8015D as the driver for its 6.5-inch hub servo motors; 7S pack 21-29.4 V is inside 20-48 V. Confirm the encoder connector (motor single-ended A/B vs driver iA+/iA-) with ZLTECH before ordering

electronics.status: Rev15: company 7S9P battery, 7-inch LCD and speaker placed from the supplied STEP files; controller, computer, drivers, power distribution are envelope reservations; DC/DC DDR-240B-24 is a size reservation (datasheet dimensions to confirm).
electronics.print_note: Rev17: LCD and speaker holders are 3D-printed (PETG/ASA); thicker sections (5 mm plate, 6 mm foot) and ribs replace the 3t steel brackets; LCD raised 3 mm onto the thicker foot. Grounding by cable to an M4 ground stud on the base plate.

battery_clamp.note: Rev17e (user): straps through base-plate slots could not be assembled; one printed clamp per battery end (x faces), 3x M5 from above per clamp into self-clinching nuts in the 3t base plate (flush, no hardware under the plate over the bogie). The rear face is boxed in by the power bay (4 mm gap) and the front face by the driver (5.6 mm), so bridges over the short side do not fit

suspension.status: Rev15 (2026-11-15): front caster + drive wheel joined by a 3t bent bogie link on each side (pivot axis +X); rear casters keep the Rev14 hinge + spring modules. The 'drive' block below is the Rev14 hinge concept, kept for history and used only when concept='hinge'. Screening calculations only.

caster.shim_note: Rev17: the bogie springs move load from the rear casters to the drive wheels (rear caster 59 -> 41 N), so the 3 mm preload shim is removed; the needed level shim would be -0.4 mm, the rear then sits about 0.6 mm high (see bogie_report rear_caster_spring)

bogie.status: Rev16: pure (unsprung) bogie. Pivot = two company-stock MISUMI BGHK6001DD-30 bearing holders hung from the base plate on one company-stock BN1359 12x35 shoulder bolt; the bolt is clamped (company-stock E-GLNUTS10 lock nut) through both ears of a 3t U bracket bolted on the bogie floor. Rotation limited by two company-stock C-USLH10 stoppers on the bogie floor against M6 striker bolts.

spring.price_seen: 2026-11-18 kr.misumi-ec.com, 1-9 pcs, VAT excl., stock 350, MOQ 1
spring.source: MISUMI SWU21-60 catalogue page 2026-11-18 (OD21 ID13.5 L60, 6.27 N/mm, allowable deflection 36). Wire section and display turns follow the SWU21-70 STEP of the same family (drawing only)
spring.note: Rev17: one compression spring per bogie, coaxial with the rear rotation stopper (C-USLH10 D10 inside, M6 striker jam nut AF10 at the top), sitting on the rear floor and pushing up on the base plate underside. 85 mm behind the pivot it pushes the drive-wheel side of the link down: more drive-wheel load (traction) and a sprung bogie (suspension)

bogie.holder_source: Supplied MISUMI STEP (user, 2026-11-15) placed unscaled; matches the catalogue table (d12 D28 B8, h30, H48, L60, L1 48, L2 36, T15, d1 5.5). Measured from the STEP: flange S10, lip D24 x 2, snap-ring mouth D28 x 5 on the other face, inner-ring land D16.3.
bogie.bolt_note: Rev17d: company-stock 12x30 (2 pcs). Collars 2.5 + 8.8 + 2 bearings 16 + outboard ear 3 = 30.3, 0.3 longer than the shoulder, so the nut clamps the ears, collars and inner rings
bogie.spacer_note: Bearing collars d12.1 x D16, length-specified catalogue collars (SKU to pick); the stack is 0.3 mm longer than the shoulder so the nut clamps the inner rings.
bogie.motor_cable_note: Rev17e (user): the 28 mm base-plate hole + grommet was removed as unnecessary. The hub-motor lead leaves the inboard axle end inside the bogie and is routed up through the wheel-well opening of the base plate beside the tire to the driver; tie it to the bogie and leave slack for the bogie stroke (route to confirm on the prototype)
bogie.holder_note: Rev17d (2026-11-19, user decision): one company-stock MISUMI BGMW6001DD-30 per side (T-type short double, h30, two 6001DD back to back in a 23 mm housing; STEP downloaded 2026-11-19) instead of two BGHK6001DD-30. Bearing centre spacing 8 mm (was 19.3) -> much higher bearing load from the roll moment; see bogie_report pivot_bearings

revision_note_rev17e: Rev17e (2026-11-20, user): motor-cable grommet removed; LiDAR scan plane matched to eco (Z206.83) on a plate-fixed printed base; camera fixed by its 2 rear M2 threads; battery held by bolted printed bridges
